10.1002_aenm.70756: Electrochromic technology has garnered significant attention for smart windows due to its dynamic solar regulation capability. However, current implementations suffer from limitations such as low optical contrast, slow switching speed, and poor cycling stability. This study addresses these challenges by designing a bipolar electrochromic architecture combining thermally‐cured WO 3 and alkoxy‐functionalized polycarbazole derivatives (CTPAO1 and CTPAO3). The optimized ECD2 (based on WO 3 and CTPAO3) achieves a comprehensive contrast of 77.4% (200–2350 nm) with a peak modulation of 87.5% at 730 nm. The device exhibits outstanding cycling stability, retaining 95% of its optical contrast after 20 000 cycles. Notably, benefiting from efficient ion transport pathways, it also shows excellent switching kinetics with a coloration time of 1.0 s and a bleaching time of 0.7 s. Building energy efficiency simulations predict that smart windows incorporating ECD2 can achieve total annual energy savings ranging from 13.1% to 50.8% across five climate zones in China. The energy‐saving effect is particularly significant in Haikou, with an estimated annual saving of 56.5 kW h/m 2 . This work provides a feasible solution for high‐performance, energy‐efficient electrochromic smart windows.
10.1016_j.ijheatmasstransfer.2026.129081: Effective thermal management remains a critical challenge in the design of lithium-ion battery packs, where non-uniform heating can degrade safety, performance, and operational lifetime. This study proposes a hierarchical, physics-informed optimization framework for battery pack cooling, integrating generative constructal design with multi-scale conjugate heat transfer simulations. The workflow addresses thermal management at three distinct levels. At the cell scale, phase change material is used to assist cooling, in combination with optimized high-conductivity annular fin structures, designed using a generative latent space approach. This reduces the number of design variables by over 95% compared to conventional pixel-wise topology optimization, while also enhancing the geometric diversity of the structures. At the module level, spatial variations in cell heating and boundary conditions are addressed by interpolating the latent space of optimized fin geometries across the cylindrical cell assembly. Functionally graded fin distributions adapt locally to thermal loads, reducing hotspot temperatures by up to 28.5% without increasing the total weight of the battery pack. This ensures improved thermal uniformity and aligns with constructal theory predictions. At the pack level, a bi-disperse porous media model is employed to optimize the cell packing density within each module, balancing hotspot temperature and pumping losses. We show that graded permeability fields can reduce hotspot temperatures by 60% compared to the lowest pumping power design, while only using 20% of the pumping power required by a uniform pack layout. The proposed generative constructal framework achieves substantial improvements in both thermal performance and computational efficiency, offering a scalable strategy for the design of safer, more energy-efficient, and longer-lasting battery systems.
10.1016_j.indcrop.2026.123352: Research on efficient adsorption and separation techniques for the core active compounds–triterpenoid acids in Jujubae Fructus is of great significance for quality control and development of functional foods in the health field. In pursuit of a selective and sustainable extraction strategy for key triterpenoid acids (betulinic acid (BA), oleanonic acid (OA), and betulonic acid (BOA)), this work developed the multi–template magnetic molecularly imprinted polymers (MMIP). A key innovation of this approach lies in the use of deep eutectic solvents (DES) as functional monomers, which are not only non-toxic and environmentally benign but also serve as effective and versatile building blocks in molecular imprinting technology (MIT). The polymer was comprehensively characterized to evaluate morphological features, crystal structure, magnetic properties, pore structure, and functional groups. The batch adsorption, selective recognition, and regeneration cycle experiments were designed to evaluate the performance characteristics of MMIP. The optimized MMIP exhibited excellent adsorption performance (Q max = 57.83 mg·g⁻¹) with high selectivity (imprinting factor = 1.39–1.48). 81.3% of the adsorption capacity of the adsorbent was maintained after seven complete adsorption–desorption cycles. When applied to Jujubae Fructus samples, the method achieved recovery rates of 82.24–91.06% (RSD < 5.76%) for BA, OA, and BOA. Our study confirmed that the developed MMIP can efficiently and selectively extract BA, OA, and BOA from complex food matrices, providing a reliable technical solution for the isolation and analysis of bioactive components in natural products.
10.1021_acs.est.6c13861: Nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) are widespread in soil and often exhibit distinct environmental behaviors and effects owing to their unique elemental composition and molecular structure. However, their toxicity to soil organisms remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, the toxicity of pristine and aged polyamides (PA) was evaluated in earthworms (Eisenia fetida), a representative soil invertebrate. At 0.01% (w/w), aged PA increased the magnitude of body-weight loss, MDA levels, and AChE activity by 24.4%, 11.6%, and 24.1%, respectively, relative to pristine PA-MPs. Greater accumulation of aged PA-MPs was accompanied by enhanced oxidative damage and neurotoxicity. Integrated multiomics, quantitative real-time PCR, and biomarker analyses revealed that oxidative stress-mediated membrane damage promoted glutamate accumulation, receptor overactivation, Ca2+ overload, synaptic injury, and ultimately neurotoxicity. Pharmacological interventions and transmission electron microscopy of the ventral nerve cord provided functional and morphological support for this cascade. Radical quenching and comparative leachate bioassays further supported the important contribution of environmentally persistent free radicals in aged PA-MPs to neuronal damage. These findings define a mechanistic pathway for aged microplastic-induced neurotoxicity and provide a basis for assessing the ecological risks of aged N-MPs in soils.
10.1039_d5ta10589g: Conventional supercapacitors are limited by their use of liquid electrolytes, which pose safety risks, leakage, stability, and flexibility issues. Herein, solid-state electrolytes with interface coatings improve contact, and ionic conductivity.
